headline_plain: Skip it: the payoff looks fine on paper, but in 10,000 replays the price almost never reached the profit goal before the safety exit.
explain_plain: The idea was to buy Nvidia today after it fell about 4.5%, hoping it bounces back before the market closes. Bull said the fall is only about worry over the boss, not the business, because every other chip company went up on Monday. Bear said the worry is still open, the price is still sliding, and surprise news about the boss can come at any minute. The news facts both sides used checked out, and Bull fixed his plan so a win pays $1.50 for every $1 he could lose. But when the desk replayed the rest of the day 10,000 times, the profit goal came first only about 3 times in 1,000, while the safety exit came first about 21 times in 100. Because the odds point toward losing, the answer is skip.
plan_plain: The trade was: buy Nvidia at about $170.70. If it fell to $166.90, sell to stop losing more (about $3.80 a share). Take profit at $176.40, then $180.20, and close everything before the market shuts today at 21:00 UTC.
retake_plain: Look again if the price climbs back above today's average price (about $172) and stays there for an hour with more and more shares trading, or if the company's board says the boss is cleared. Then the desk's replays would also need to show the profit goal coming first about as often as the safety exit.
summary: Bull's final plan (170.70 / 166.90 / 176.40, 180.20) passes the desk's 1.5R reward rule and the stop is ~1x 1h ATR (0.99x, stop_tight warn), but the Time Machine is STRONG_STOP: 0.33% target-first vs 21.4% stop-first, avg -0.31R, history 0/59 target vs 6/59 stop. Bear also wins the scorecard 27-22, so two TAKE conditions fail. SKIP.
reasoning:
Two TAKE gates fail. First, the scorecard: Bull 22 vs Bear 27, so Bull does not beat Bear at all, let alone by 3. Second and decisive, desk_r3 Time Machine on the final plan (entry 170.70, stop 166.90, T1 176.40, T2 180.20, 315-minute window to the close): target-first 0.33%, stop-first 21.38%, neither 78.3%, avg R -0.307, P(green at close) 28.9%; real history 0 target / 6 stop / 53 neither of 59. Lean STRONG_STOP. At 1.5R the target needs ~40% of decided paths; it got ~2%.

The other gates pass or nearly pass: desk R multiples 1.5 and 2.5; stop 0.99x the 1h ATR (3.8564), flagged stop_tight but at the ~1x threshold; market open with fresh data; events.json CLEAR (only tier-3 macro). Live re-check at 15:44Z: 170.31 (-4.68%), day low 170.12 intact, entry 170.70 reachable. 1h RSI 26.8, 1h MACD histogram -0.47 and still falling, EMA9 < EMA21 on 5m/15m/1h, price below session VWAP 172.03. No sign of a turn.

Fact checks: the Yahoo article confirms NVDA was the only chip stock down Monday (close 178.62, -4.3%), AMD ~+4%, Broadcom ~+3%, SOX 'more than 6.8%', and the board probe. The Yahoo UK article confirms IG +432%, HL 8:1, II +274%, but gives no institutional data, so Bull's 'institutions also buying' is anecdotal. Bull's R3 errors: stop 1.04x ATR (desk 0.99x) and his own replay (0.2% / 14.1%) understated the stop-first rate (desk 21.4%); R1 used the 5m ATR. Bear's R3 numbers described Bull's R2 plan (stale) but the conclusion holds on the final plan. Bull's honesty in R3 was credited; his case rests on an unscheduled fear-fade catalyst the data does not show.

key_risks_plain: In 10,000 practice replays the profit goal almost never came first, but the safety exit often did.
Surprise news about the boss could come at any time and move the price fast.
The price is still going down on every chart and is below today's average price.
The safety exit is only about one normal hourly wiggle away, so ordinary moves could hit it.
A bounce could still happen, but nothing in the data shows it starting yet.
